command: claude CLI 2.1.285 print mode (claude -p --model claude-opus-5-5 --effort high --tools '' --strict-mcp-config --mcp-config '{"mcpServers":{}}' --no-session-persistence --system-prompt <porting system prompt>, prompt file on stdin, run from an empty directory)
notes:
Fix for attempt 1: HANDLE ABEND LABEL, PUSH HANDLE and POP HANDLE now go through the task (task.handleAbend /
pushHandle / popHandle). Before, the exit was only a local flag, so an abend raised in HCSUB could not find
HCMAIN's exit one level up. After the LINK, the port reads task.abendExit() / task.ended(). An unhandled
condition goes through task.abendOnCondition. No exception is caught or thrown to model a CICS transfer.

Defects of the original kept as they are:
- MAIN-ABEND strings CA-TRAIL(1:3) even when WS-CA was never INITIALIZEd. This happens when the abend comes
  from the HCMODE read, for example LENGERR on an item longer than WS-MLEN = 1. The trail then holds WS-CA's
  initial binary zeros. Fix: INITIALIZE WS-CA at the top of MAIN-PARA.
- WS-JLEN is never reset. After the line-37 read it holds that item's length, and the line-54 read uses it
  as its maximum. That can raise LENGERR (unhandled, so AEIV goes to MAIN-ABEND) for an item longer than
  the first one. Fix: MOVE 8 TO WS-JLEN before each READQ.
- In 'P' mode the line-37 READQ runs with every handler suspended by PUSH HANDLE. A missing HCNONE queue
  therefore terminates the task with AEYH, and neither MAIN-QIDERR nor MAIN-ABEND takes it. This is kept
  as the program intends.

Facts found contradicted:
- commarea_contracts says the caller's record WS-CA is 4 bytes, 1 field, with a shape mismatch against
  HCSUB's DFHCOMMAREA. The source has WS-CA as COPY HCLINKCA, the same 20-byte, 5-field layout that HCSUB
  declares. The port follows the source and passes the HcsubDfhcommarea DTO unchanged, with LENGTH(20).
